candidates.title: Probing the Prompt KV Cache: Where It Becomes Dispensable
candidates.abstract: Prior KV cache compression schemes empirically demonstrate that the prompt cache is partially redundant during decoding, dropping or summarising entries with little accuracy loss. We ask when and what kind of redundancy: at which layers, after how many decoding steps, and in what form can the prompt span KV cache be replaced without breaking the task. A controlled splice intervention swept over layer cutoff and decoding steps shows this redundancy is about form (chat template scaffolding) rather than content. Replacing the upper layer prompt span KV cache with KV cache from a chat template scaffold whose user content is a neutral filler recovers near clean accuracy, while zeroing the same slots collapses accuracy. The dissociation replicates across the Qwen3, Gemma 3, and Llama 3 families on multiple datasets.
candidates.reason: プロンプトKVキャッシュを層と復号ステップ別に差し替える介入実験で、上層の冗長性が内容ではなくチャットテンプレート形式に由来することを示す。中立的なユーザー内容を持つテンプレート由来KVへの置換は精度を概ね回復する一方、ゼロ埋めでは精度が崩壊。Qwen3、Gemma 3、Llama 3で再現。KVキャッシュ圧縮設計への直接的知見。
